newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar follows bonds to close softer.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar follows bonds to close softer.

text.p: * Canada's dollar followed weakening Canadian bond prices to close softer in quiet trading at C$1.3578 (US$0.7365) from Monday's close at C$1.3550 (US$0.7380), dealers said. * They said market players were also unnerved by published reports suggesting Canada had a persistent unemployment problem despite restructuring in the economy.
Ontario Hydro announced a C$2.5 billion charge after the market close on Tuesday, but rumors hit the currency market in afternoon trading, dealers said.

A confidential IMF report concluding that Canada had a persistent unemployment problem despite major progress in restructuring the economy also bothered investors, dealers said. The Toronto Globe and Mail published a story about the report today.
Another report by economists at CIBC Wood Gundy suggested a sharp rise in the Canadian currency would drive the current account surplus into a defict.
That report also helped soften the Canadian dollar, traders said.
"The market just kind of senses something is coming up," said one trader.
Volume was light heading into the holiday season, dealers said. They said most of the market interest came from Canadian corporations.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar eased to 1.1426 marks from Monday's close at 1.1492 marks and slid to 83.40 yen from 83.67 yen.
